Sensors tell you something moved.
Only behavior tells you what it's doing.

A radar return, an AIS ping and a seismic trigger all report the same thing: a contact exists. None of them, alone, says whether it matters. Vanguard 26's engine scores movement pattern against context — speed, heading persistence, loiter, approach geometry — the same behavioral logic across every domain, retrained on the signal vocabulary of each one.

That's why a bird, a drifting fishing boat and a patrol vehicle all get filtered before an operator ever sees them, while a quadcopter holding station over a fence line, a vessel going dark near a rig, or a figure pacing a border segment all get flagged — before impact, not after.

One intelligence layer. Multiple missions.

Kernel, Marlin and Lynx share roughly 70% of their code — the same sensor-fusion, scoring and alerting pipeline, retrained per domain. That is what let three products reach this accuracy in one build cycle instead of three.

01 — INGEST

Take the sensors as they are

Radar, RF, EO/IR, acoustic, AIS, ADS-B, seismic and ground cameras normalise through adapters into one contact format. No rip-and-replace on site.

02 — FUSE

One contact, not five

Returns from different sensors describing the same object merge into a single track with a continuous kinematic history.

03 — SCORE

Score the behavior

Kinematics, signature and movement pattern feed a confidence-scored classification the operator can audit feature by feature.

04 — DECIDE

Route it to a response

Thresholds and rules of engagement hand the track to the customer's existing C2, VMS or dispatch — every decision written to an append-only log.

Three products, one core.

Kernel is the current build; Marlin and Lynx extend the same fusion core, data model and audit layer into maritime and ground domains.

{{ p.label }}
AIRIN BUILD

Kernel

A command layer for drone detection and response. Fuses radar, RF direction-finding, EO/IR and Remote ID into one track file per object, classifies it against six behavior classes, and cues the response before an operator has to ask what they are looking at.

96.1%classification accuracy
100%threat recall
6behavior classes
SENSORSRF detection · pulse-Doppler radar · EO/IR · ADS-B · acoustic arrays
BOUGHT BYAirport authorities · base security · critical infrastructure

Fuses what you already own

Radar, RF, EO/IR, acoustic and Remote ID feeds normalise into a single track — two sensors seeing the same drone produce one contact, not two alarms.

Separates threat from clutter

Flight behaviour and signal signature together distinguish a quadcopter from a bird, a balloon or a returning airliner, so operators are only woken for contacts that matter.

Cues the response

On classification, Kernel slews cameras, opens video, logs an evidentiary record, and hands the track to an existing VMS, PSIM or command network through modular APIs.

SEANEXT

Marlin

A maritime picture built on AIS ingestion cross-checked against radar and behavior scoring. Separates ordinary fishing, transit and loitering traffic from the small share of tracks that warrant a closer look — dark transits, rendezvous patterns, and course changes near restricted water.

91.7%classification accuracy
90.3%threat recall
7behavior classes
SENSORSCoastal radar · AIS · satellite AIS · EO/IR masts · hydrophones
BOUGHT BYPort authorities · coast guards · offshore operators

Reads real AIS traffic

Built and validated against live Marine Cadastre AIS data, not synthetic tracks alone — the engine has seen what ordinary vessel behaviour actually looks like.

Tuned to vessel class

Tugs, trawlers, tankers and pleasure craft carry different baseline behaviour; Marlin scores deviation from each class's own norm rather than one generic threshold.

Flags the exception, not the ordinary

81% of tracked contacts on a typical day are stationary or in routine transit — Marlin's job is finding the minority pattern that isn't, and saying why.

LANDNEXT

Lynx

A border and perimeter classification layer that turns seismic, thermal and camera triggers into a scored track instead of a raw alarm. Built for long, thin coverage lines where sensors are sparse, staffing is thin, and every false alarm has a real cost in attention.

95.7%classification accuracy
94.8%threat recall
7behavior classes
SENSORSGround radar · seismic and fibre lines · thermal cameras · RF survey
BOUGHT BYBorder forces · energy corridors · correctional facilities

Holds contacts through gaps

Predictive tracking carries a track across sensor blind spots instead of dropping it, so a crossing pattern is still visible on the other side of a gap in coverage.

Separates wildlife from people

Gait, pacing and group behaviour distinguish human crossing patterns from animal movement, the single largest source of nuisance alarms on a rural line.

Builds a pattern-of-life record

Recurring crossing points and timing are logged over time, showing where a route is being used repeatedly rather than reporting each event in isolation.

Built on components a customer can inspect.

The core is assembled from permissively licensed open source, with our own work in fusion, classification and the operator layer. Buyers can audit the dependency tree; nothing in the chain forces disclosure of customer configurations.

Track fusion and state estimationKalman / IMM · Apache-2.0
Message transport between nodesNATS / MQTT · Apache-2.0
Track and event storePostgreSQL + TimescaleDB
Classification runtimeONNX Runtime · MIT
Geospatial enginePostGIS / PROJ
Operator mapMapLibre GL · BSD-3
Signal and RF processingNumPy / SciPy · BSD
Audit and integrity logappend-only · hash-chained
Deploymentcontainers · air-gap capable
Our layerkernel-core · proprietary

Edge node

A single rugged box beside the sensor mast. Classifies locally, keeps working when the link drops, syncs when it returns.

On-premise cluster

Site or national control room, fully air-gapped. Updates delivered as signed offline bundles.

Sovereign cloud

Customer-controlled tenancy for multi-site operators who need one picture across regions, with data residency written into the contract.

Detection and classification only. Vanguard produces tracks, classifications and alerts. It does not interfere with, disable or engage any aircraft, vessel or vehicle. Where a customer operates mitigation equipment, that is done by authorised parties under the laws of their jurisdiction, and Vanguard integrates with it only where such authority exists.

Where it goes in.

The same engine, tuned to the threat model and the sensor mix a site already has.

Bases and forward sites

Persistent coverage over fixed installations and rapid setup for deployed positions, with a fused picture shared across the command chain.

Ports and coastal infrastructure

Terminals and anchorages where a single incursion stops production — continuous monitoring with an audit trail suitable for regulators and insurers.

Borders and coastline

Long, thin coverage areas where sensors are sparse and false alarms are expensive. Predictive tracking holds contacts through gaps.

Correctional facilities

Contraband delivery by drone or on foot is a nightly, repeating pattern — Lynx and Kernel log it over time to show where deliveries originate.

Airports and energy sites

Verified detection near approach corridors and substations, integrating with existing tower, PSIM and security workflows rather than replacing them.

PLATFORM THESIS

One platform. Multiple mission systems.

Shared data models, fusion, classification and audit layers form one technical foundation across Kernel, Marlin and Lynx — each new domain is an extension of engineering already paid for, not a second company.

01 / LAND & EXPAND

Start with one mission.

Kernel establishes the shared architecture and the first reference deployments. Additional domains are roadmap extensions rather than separate technical foundations.

02 / REUSABLE CORE

Reuse the hard part.

Fusion, track state, audit and operator infrastructure are common layers. Roughly 70% of code is shared, so marginal cost per domain falls as the library of behavior classes grows.

03 / SOFTWARE MODEL

License the intelligence layer.

Recurring software licensing over customer-owned sensors and customer-controlled infrastructure — edge, on-premise or sovereign cloud — in markets where data residency is contractual.

SCALE PATH

Kernel first. Marlin and Lynx next.

01 / FOUNDATION

Unify the track

Normalise heterogeneous sensor feeds into one persistent contact and event model with an auditable history.

02 / INTELLIGENCE

Deepen behavioral classification

03 / PLATFORM

Deploy across sites and domains

Carry the same architecture from a single edge node to multi-site sovereign infrastructure across the Americas and the Gulf.
